title: Latency fingerprinting per-token + KV-cache sensitivity telemetry
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce lightweight per-token latency 'fingerprints' emitted by the serving runtime and correlated metadata for KV cache hits/misses. Objective is to enable accurate attribution of latency and token-level cost to upstream customers and internal billing, surface KV-cache sensitivity for model variants, and provide dashboards/alerts for regressions. This ticket covers design, runtime probes, OTLP/metrics export, aggregation jobs, and Grafana dashboarding. Goal: high-fidelity attribution while keeping runtime overhead <3% p50 CPU and <1% p95 tail increase for hot paths.
background: Current token-attribution work surfaces request-level token counts and a small set of micro-timings. We still lack a deterministic mapping between emission timings and cache hit semantics across model families (e.g., kv-split when using optimized kernels), and dashboards cannot isolate which subtokens drive tail latency. Prior incidents (INC-2025-09-12) showed a cache-eviction storm causing 30% tail latency spikes for a large customer — root cause analysis was limited by coarse-grain metrics. This work responds to that gap.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits per-token timing events with schema (token_index, model_variant, step, latency_ms, kv_hit:boolean, cache_tier:string, request_id) in OTLP spans or a compact event stream
Metrics pipeline ingests token events and generates aggregated views: per-model per-sequence-length p50/p95/p99 token latency, kv-hit vs kv-miss delta histograms, and cost-attribution reports
Grafana dashboard created: Token Fingerprint explorer with trace-linking to individual requests and a KV-sensitivity heatmap
End-to-end test harness and synthetic load show <3% p50 CPU overhead and <1% p95 tail regression for production 99th-percentile path
Documentation (Confluence) with data retention, schema, and privacy notes published
One Canary rollout completed to a subset of Dedicated customers and validation queries confirm no customer-visible regressions
implementation_plan: Design: finalise event schema and sampling policy (full emit for small requests, 1/N sampling for large streaming requests)
Runtime: add lightweight hook in emission loop to stamp token events and attach kv-cache flag; implement C++ fast-path and fallback SDK shim for Private deployments
Tracing: map token events to OpenTelemetry spans with attribute keys prefixed rw.token.*; include trace_id->request_id correlation
Metrics pipeline: add new collector job that ingests OTLP event stream, enriches with model metadata (from model-catalog), and writes rollups to BigQuery and Prometheus-compatible exporter
Dashboards: build Grafana dashboard panels and a LogQL query for KV-hit delta analysis
Testing: microbench harness, integration tests for schema changes, and canary job to validate overhead and false-positive rates for alerts
Rollout: staged canary (5% traffic) -> 25% -> 100% with rollback playbook
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deploy on runtime canaries. 2) Enable full event emission for internal sandbox and Dedicated customers opted-in. 3) Run data validation job for 24h, compare aggregate counters vs baseline. 4) Gradual expansion to hosted tenants with opt-in controls and config knobs for sampling rate. 5) Post-rollout: run 72h anomaly detection job on kv-sensitivity metrics and open follow-ups if deviation >15% from baseline.
risks_mitigation: Risk: High cardinality of token events could overwhelm metrics pipeline. Mitigation: strict sampling policy, compact binary wire format, and on-ingest dedupe/aggregation windows (e.g., 1s buckets)

Risk: Sensitive user content in token payloads. Mitigation: only emit token_index and hashed token fingerprint; do not include raw token text in production telemetry. Documented in Confluence with privacy review notes.
Risk: Runtime overhead causing tail regressions. Mitigation: implement hot-path fast-path in C++ with approximate timers and run microbench before enabling for production tenants.
Risk: Billing attribution mismatch. Mitigation: add reconciliation job that cross-checks token counts with billing ledger weekly and flags drift >0.5%
